findings.title: getBaseConditions can return an un-parenthesized top-level OR, breaking AND-composition by callers
findings.body: `getBaseConditions()` returns the authorization SQL verbatim when there are no filters (line 75), and for `org`/`team` scope that SQL is a top-level `OR` expression such as `("teamId" = ANY($1)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true) OR (("userId" = ANY($2)) AND ("isTeamBooking" = false))` with no surrounding parentheses (see the reduce at lines 171-174 and 204-207). Any consumer that interpolates the result into a larger predicate, e.g. ``WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ${from}``, gets `A AND B OR (C AND D AND startTime>=...)` because `AND` binds tighter than `OR`. That silently returns bookings outside the requested date range and, worse, rows that should have been excluded by the additional predicate — an authorization-scope leak. The same applies to the public `getFilterConditions()`, which returns `("eventTypeId" = $1) OR ("eventParentId" = $1)` unwrapped when it is the only filter. All returned fragments should be wrapped in outer parentheses (e.g. `Prisma.sql`(${expr})`).

findings.title: Public findMany() removed without updating any callers
findings.body: The `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` method was deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment instead of executing a query. No other file in the repository is touched by this PR, so any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (e.g. insights tRPC routers/handlers) will fail to compile or, if dynamically typed, fail at runtime. Either keep `findMany` as a thin wrapper that runs `$queryRaw` with the base conditions, or update all call sites in the same change.

findings.title: Loosened constructor option type lets invalid scopes compile and silently degrade to 1=0
findings.body: The constructor now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (`scope: "user" | "org" | "team"`, `teamId?: number`) instead of the discriminated union `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`. Previously, passing `scope: "team"` without a `teamId` was a compile error; now it type-checks, zod validation fails in the constructor, `this.options` becomes `null`, and every query silently gets the `1=0` condition with no error or log. A caller mis-wiring the options will see an empty insights result set rather than a failure, which is very hard to diagnose. Keep the discriminated union in the constructor signature, or at minimum throw/log when `safeParse` fails.

findings.title: Caching tests for auth/filter conditions were deleted while the caching logic remains
findings.body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block (tests for `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`) was removed, but `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` in the service still memoize via `this.cachedAuthConditions`/`this.cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts lines 83-95). Notably the `null` case for filter conditions is a subtle memoization branch (`undefined` vs `null`) that is now completely untested, so a regression that re-queries the DB on every call, or that caches `null` incorrectly, would go unnoticed. The tests should be ported to the new SQL expectations rather than dropped.

findings.title: Only the user-scope SQL is actually executed against the database; ANY() array binding is untested
findings.body: The only test that runs real SQL (`$queryRaw` on `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`) uses `scope: "user"`, whose condition contains no arrays. The org and team scope conditions rely on `"teamId" = ANY(${array})` / `"userId" = ANY(${array})` parameter binding (insightsBooking.ts lines 164, 168, 201), which is only asserted by structural `toEqual` comparison of `Prisma.Sql` objects — that cannot catch a failure of the driver to bind a JS array as a Postgres array, nor a column-type mismatch. Add integration tests that execute the org- and team-scope base conditions via `$queryRaw` and assert the returned rows.

findings.title: Org-scope assertion depends on unordered query results, making the test flaky
findings.body: The expectation compares the exact bound-parameter arrays `[org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]` against the SQL built from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`. Those repository calls have no `orderBy`, so PostgreSQL may return rows in any order; since `toEqual` on a `Prisma.Sql` compares the `values` array element-by-element, the test can fail non-deterministically. Either sort the ids in the service before building the condition or compare order-insensitively (e.g. assert on sorted copies of `conditions.values`).
